answer: Persistent Identity Graph (PIG) enforces cross-epoch consistency by requiring identity graphs built in earlier epochs to harbor verifiable connection patterns that validate new epoch actions, with deviation triggering cascading verification costs. A sybil attacker must maintain consistent graph structures across epochs or pay exponentially increasing computational and financial costs to rebuild credibility at each inlet where prior inconsistencies are detected. The vault of validated historical interactions then locks compromised identities from further epoch progression.
